text:
Rafael Mendes: starting a thread for early retro/postmortem notes on the pilot incident. please dump facts here while it’s fresh + links.

Incident Bot: Reminder: For postmortems, capture impact, detection, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, mitigation, follow-ups, and “where we got lucky”. Template: go/postmortem-template (internal)

Vanessa Ortiz: link to incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/incidents/p1709135111 (Bootstrapping stuck -> Ready inconsistently set)

Vanessa Ortiz: tl;dr from my view: during pilot pool expansion, some runs hit a state machine edge where routing saw pool “Ready” briefly while validation/perf-canary was still running. we caught it fast and pulled the pool out of routing, but it caused a short window of 5xx for internal test traffic + scared everyone.

Ravi Menon: +1. routing side: we only consume control-plane Ready. the bug was Ready being set before perf-canary completion in one code path. when capacity got advertised, a subset of requests went to nodes still warming / helm not fully converged.

Ethan Park: control-plane notes:
- state transition sequence should be: Requested -> Provisioning -> Imaging -> Bootstrapping -> Validating -> Ready
- we had a race: Validating stage emitted “done” on smoke checks, and Ready transition happened before perf-canary callback wrote its final status
- specifically: perf-canary runs async; we didn’t enforce transactional check on “canary_passed == true” before Ready write

Gabe Wilson: PR that fixes the race is up + merged: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/48245
Adds a guard: Ready write requires perf_canary_status=PASS and validates run_id matches latest attempt. Also adds a test that reproduces the out-of-order callback.

Miles Thornton: contributing factor: retries + stage re-run made it more likely. we had:
- validation rerun (stage-only) while older perf-canary job still finishing
- older job callback arrived late and updated status unexpectedly
We should call out idempotency + “latest attempt wins” semantics.

Allison Grant: observability gap we should mention: dashboard made it look like pool was Ready for ~6m but we didn’t have an alert for “Ready while perf_canary_status != PASS”. we only page on “stuck stage” / “failure rate”.
Action item: add invariant metric + alert (non-paging ticket might be fine).

Connor O'Brien: release angle: we enabled the feature flag for the pilot window while also merging a couple of other provisioning changes. we didn’t have a crisp rollback playbook for “Ready semantics bug” other than manually pulling pool from routing.
Maybe follow-up: add explicit kill-switch in routing integration to ignore Ready if validating fields aren’t satisfied (belt + suspenders).

Kira Thompson: runbook gap: operator steps didn’t say what to check when control plane shows Ready but perf-canary still running. folks were grepping logs in 3 places.
I can add a section to the “control-plane ready state troubleshooting” doc + link the exact queries.

Rafael Mendes: quick draft facts (please correct):
- Impact: internal pilot traffic saw intermittent 5xx + elevated latency; no customer traffic should’ve hit it (pool was not in customer routing policy), but it did show up in shared staging validation runs.
- Detection: humans in #eng-oncall noticed validation errors + routing metrics blip; no automated alert fired.
- Duration: ~10–15 min from first blip to mitigation (manual remove from routing + pause provisioning runs)
- Mitigation: force routing to ignore pool, then rerun validation, then resume once perf-canary completed.

Vanessa Ortiz: timeline-ish (approx, we can pull exact from events once Logan backfills):
- T0: provisioning run enters Validating
- T0+?m: perf-canary launched
- T0+?m: smoke checks pass and Ready set (bug)
- T0+?m: routing advertises pool, internal reqs start landing
- T0+?m: errors show up (helm still converging + runtime not warmed)
- T0+?m: pool removed from routing, runs paused
- T0+?m: PR 48245 merged + redeploy control plane

Ethan Park: note: we should be explicit that “Ready” was used as a contract boundary across systems (control plane -> routing). once we violate it, the downstream behavior was correct (it assumed Ready meant safe).
Action: strengthen Ready contract + add invariants tested in CI.

Ravi Menon: +1. also action: routing should consider exposing a “readiness gate reason” in metrics when it refuses capacity, so if we add the extra belt it’s observable (avoid silent capacity drop).

Allison Grant: proposal for alerts:
- invariant: count of pools where state=Ready AND perf_canary_status!=PASS > 0 for 5m -> ticket in #eng-sre
- stage event: out-of-order callback detected (we log it now) -> low-sev warning + counter

Miles Thornton: “where we got lucky”: pilot pool was small + mostly internal traffic; if this had been a customer expansion window it could’ve violated SLA.
Also lucky we had manual override + someone watching #eng-infra live.

Gabe Wilson: follow-up ideas (engineering):
- make perf-canary synchronous for readiness mode (block state machine) OR keep async but require lease/attempt token
- add a state machine property-based test for out-of-order events (we have one unit test now but it’s narrow)

Kira Thompson: I’ll draft runbook updates and post for review:
- “If Ready set but canary pending” checks
- commands to query run status by correlation_id
- how to safely “pause/resume” and re-run Validating only

Connor O'Brien: can someone own pulling exact timestamps from structured events for the retro? I think Logan/Caleb can do it but if they’re out, I can query from logs.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll ping Logan. For now, everyone: if you remember any exact error strings / screenshots / links, drop them here.

Vanessa Ortiz: error we saw a few times (from operator CLI): `routing_advertised=true but canary_status=PENDING` (after the fix it should never happen; before fix it was a clue)
Also we should link PR that added transactional check + mention regression test.

Incident Bot: Action items mentioned in thread so far:
- Add invariant alert: Ready && perf_canary_status!=PASS (owner: Allison)
- Update runbooks for Ready vs canary pending (owner: Kira)
- Consider routing belt-and-suspenders gate (owner: Ravi)
- Pull exact timeline from structured events (owner: Rafael/Logan)
- Expand state machine tests for out-of-order callbacks (owner: Gabe/Ethan)

Rafael Mendes: thanks. I’ll copy this into the retro doc later today + we’ll review in the postmortem meeting. keep adding anything you think we’ll forget.
